Consider the region $D$ shown above. If 

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D,\end{aligned}
$$

 
which of the following statements are true?

- ${∬}_{D}x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,\,$ where $R=[-1,1]\times [-2,3]$
- ${∬}_{R}x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A={∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,\,$ where $R=[-3,3]\times [-3,3]$
- ${∬}_{D}x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,\,$ where $R=[-2,2]\times [-3,3]$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that if $R$ covers $D$ completely and we define 

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D,\end{aligned}
$$

we obtain

$$
{∬}_{D}x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine each of the given statements.

- Statement I is false. The rectangle $R$ does not cover the region $D.$

- Statement II is false. The integrals have not been stated correctly with respect to the domains $R$ and $D$ (they have been swapped).

- Statement III is true. The rectangle $R$ covers the region $D$ completely.

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."
